solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Boxing Day is rough for him

indicators.note: boxing something in means enclosing it, so one word goes around the other

parts.note: rough seas are wild seas
Fri is the short form of Friday, a day of the week

explanation.surface: A man whose Boxing Day is a hard time, perhaps after too much Christmas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boxing Day' looks like the festive holiday, but 'Boxing' is the container signal. 'him' is a bare pointer to a man's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A male first name is the kind of person the pronoun stands for; Wilfrid is a man's name.

clue.text: Employer's argument over fluctuating markets

indicators.note: in a down clue, over means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: a row is a heated argument

indicators.note: fluctuating means shifting, so these letters shift into a new order

explanation.surface: A boss's quarrel about markets going up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for a foreman or boss who sets people to work, an employer.

clue.text: Be grumpy about opening fresh claret in flat

indicators.note: the turned word opens up the jumbled letters by going into them
fresh letters are a new arrangement of the old ones
about means turned around, read backwards

parts.note: to sulk is to be grumpy

explanation.surface: Someone sulking about a freshly opened claret that has gone flat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' gives KLUS; 'fresh' makes LACTRE; 'opening' puts the first inside the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Something lacklustre lacks sparkle or energy, so it is dull and lifeless.

clue.text: Parts of salad preparation perversely burn pots

indicators.note: to pot something is to put it in a pot, so one word holds the other
perversely means the wrong way round, read backwards

parts.note: to sear is to burn
a dish is a food preparation

explanation.surface: A salad cook somehow burns the pots while making it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pots' looks like cookware but is the container signal, and 'perversely' gives RAES.
explanation.definitionFit: Radishes are crisp red root vegetables often eaten raw as part of a salad.

clue.text: Snobbish fool leaves instruction to identify Countdown format

indicators.note: the fool leaves, departing from the longer word

parts.note: condescending means snobbish and patronising
to con someone is to fool them
an order is an instruction

explanation.surface: A snooty idiot leaves orders on how to spot the TV show's format.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes CON out of CONDESCENDING. Countdown is a British TV quiz with a clock; the answer is a counting-down sequence.
explanation.definitionFit: A countdown runs from high numbers to low, the arrangement of items from largest to smallest.

clue.text: Cut turkey sandwiches are the thing for starters

indicators.note: to sandwich something is to hold it between two parts, so one word encloses the others

parts.note: a turkey is a show or product that fails, a flop

indicators.note: starters are the opening letters of each of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Carving the turkey and making sandwiches is the first job at the Christmas meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turkey' reads as the Christmas bird but means a failure; 'sandwiches' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat-top is a style of haircut, a cut with the hair short and level on the crown.

clue.text: Simple bed where mathematician pens articles — rest's disturbed

indicators.note: to pen something is to shut it in, so one word encloses the others

parts.note: Pierre de Fermat was a French mathematician
a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article

indicators.note: disturbed letters are moved around into a new order

parts.note: rest's stands for rest is, giving the letters of both words

explanation.surface: A basic bed where a mathematician writes papers while his rest is interrupted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pens' looks like writing but means encloses; 'disturbed' makes TRESS.
explanation.definitionFit: A mattress stuffed with feathers was the plain, old-fashioned bed before springs.

clue.text: Full ration, superior parts

indicators.note: the letter parts the other word, splitting it to sit inside

parts.note: to allot is to ration out shares
U stands for upper class, socially superior

explanation.surface: A complete ration of the better cuts of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' looks like a noun but is a verb: U parts ALLOT. U is the old British label for upper-class usage.
explanation.definitionFit: An all-out effort holds nothing back, so it is total and complete.

clue.text: Temperature's utterly unbelievable

parts.note: T is the abbreviation for temperature
all can mean utterly, as in all alone

explanation.surface: The temperature is completely beyond belief.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall story is one too far-fetched to be believed.

clue.text: Sweep outside with this tool

indicators.note: the sweeping word sits outside the other, enclosing it

parts.note: to pan a camera is to sweep it across a scene

explanation.surface: A cleaning instruction: sweep outdoors using this implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweep' suggests a broom, but it is a camera's movement, PAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A pawn is a person used by others for their own ends, a mere tool.

clue.text: Was runner one finding a way round?

indicators.note: the way goes round the one, enclosing it

parts.note: RD is the abbreviation for road, a way
an ace is a one in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Asks whether a runner was simply someone looking for a way around an obstacle.
explanation.definitionFit: To have raced is to have taken part in a race, as a runner did.

clue.text: Thus traffic is all snarled up in winter weather?

indicators.note: the jumbled letters are placed in the weather word

parts.note: snow is typical weather in winter

indicators.note: snarled-up letters are tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Traffic is all snarled up in winter weather, crawling along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'snarled up' makes AILSL, and 'in' puts it inside the weather word.
explanation.definitionFit: Traffic held up in snow moves at a crawl, the pace of a snail.

clue.text: Speed, as in amphetamine, reduced

parts.note: the letters MPH sit inside amphetamine, the drug called speed; cut down to those letters, it is the usual short form of a rate of speed

explanation.surface: A note about speed meaning amphetamine, in its reduced form.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speed' looks like the slang name for amphetamine, but the clue wants the letters MPH inside that word, the abbreviation, given here in full.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed on the road is measured as a distance covered in a set time, written MPH.

clue.text: Mafia stalwarts, on a society holding them back

indicators.note: back means the held letters are read in the reverse direction
the words hold the letters within them, spanning the word breaks

explanation.surface: Loyal members of the Mafia, belonging to a society that keeps them in check.
explanation.walkthrough: 'holding' takes ARTSONASOC from 'stalwarts, on a society'; 'back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: The Italian phrase, 'our thing', is the name used for the Sicilian and American crime syndicate.

clue.text: Spat on privileged person's typical Christmas gift

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece on another sits above it

parts.note: afters is football slang for a scuffle after a tackle, a spat
a have is a privileged person, as in the haves and have-nots

explanation.surface: Someone spits on a privileged person's usual Christmas present.
explanation.walkthrough: In British football slang, 'afters' is a bit of pushing and shoving after a foul.
explanation.definitionFit: Bottles of scented lotion for men are a standard present at Christmas.

clue.text: Without us they'll splash out on some underwear

indicators.note: without here means outside, so the spending word goes around the other

parts.note: spenders are people who will splash out money

explanation.surface: Shoppers without us will lavish money on lingerie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' seems to mean 'lacking', but here it has its old sense 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain these are garters for stockings, a kind of underwear; in the US the word means braces.

clue.text: Animal seen in winter or late fall, primarily

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of each of the words after it

explanation.surface: A creature that is spotted in winter or in late autumn.
explanation.definitionFit: The wolf is a wild member of the dog family, a kind of animal.

clue.text: Excellent Christmas tree to entertain domestic goddess

indicators.note: to entertain guests is to have them inside, so one word holds the other

parts.note: a fir is the usual Christmas tree
Vesta was the Roman goddess of the hearth and home

explanation.surface: A fine Christmas tree to put on a show for a skilled home cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'domestic goddess' suggests a celebrity cook, but it is Vesta, the Roman goddess of the household.
explanation.definitionFit: A five-star rating is the highest, given to hotels or reviews that are outstanding.

clue.text: Draw close, but heading to the back

indicators.note: the heading, the word's opening letter, moves to the end

parts.note: near means close by

explanation.surface: Come nearer, but walk towards the rear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw close' reads as one phrase meaning approach; split it. NEAR has its head letter moved to the back.
explanation.definitionFit: To draw a salary is to receive pay for work, so draw and earn are synonyms.

clue.text: Void data in live broadcast

indicators.note: seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters are scattered too

explanation.surface: Data gathered during a live broadcast is no good.
explanation.definitionFit: To void something, such as a contract, is to cancel it so it has no legal force.

clue.text: Advent calendar's opening outside home is incredible

indicators.note: the opening of a word is its first letter
the exclamation sits outside the other word, enclosing it

parts.note: OMG, 'oh my God', is said of something incredible
in means at home

explanation.surface: Opening an Advent calendar while out of the house is amazing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Advent calendar' reads as one thing, but 'Advent' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Advent means an arrival, from Latin for coming to, as in the coming of Christmas.

clue.text: Best Father Christmas tradition on TV

definitions.meaning: the finest of all dads: top meaning best, pops meaning fathers
the BBC's long-running pop chart show had a Christmas Day edition every year

explanation.surface: Praise for the greatest Father Christmas of all, on the telly.
explanation.walkthrough: This was a British weekly TV show of the pop charts; its Christmas Day special kept running after the weekly show stopped.
explanation.definitionFit: Read literally the title is the highest of the dads; it is also the name of a festive broadcast.

clue.text: It sparkles during Christmas time

indicators.note: during means the answer occurs in the middle of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something festive fizzes over the Christmas period.
explanation.definitionFit: Asti is a sparkling white wine from the Piedmont region of Italy.

clue.text: Spanish wine (OK, French)

parts.note: ça va is French for 'it's OK', the first word giving ca
the second word of the French phrase ça va gives va

explanation.surface: Spanish wine is fine, says a Frenchman.
explanation.walkthrough: The French phrase ça va, 'it's going fine', written without its accent, spells the wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Cava is a sparkling wine made in Catalonia in Spain.

clue.text: Marine growth dies with large waves

indicators.note: the letters move like waves, rearranging

explanation.surface: Something growing in the sea dies when big waves come.
explanation.walkthrough: 'waves' looks like part of the sea scene but tells you to rearrange DIES and LARGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sea girdle is a name for a kind of kelp, a seaweed that grows in the ocean.

clue.text: It indicates "four" soldiers are on the offensive

indicators.note: in an across clue, one piece placed on another follows it

parts.note: the Tet Offensive was a campaign in the Vietnam War
RA is the Royal Artillery, a body of soldiers

explanation.surface: A military order: soldiers marked 'four' are going on the attack.
explanation.walkthrough: TET is the Vietnamese New Year, best known from the 1968 Tet Offensive. 'four' looks like a unit label but is what the answer means.
explanation.definitionFit: Tetra- is the Greek prefix for four, as in tetrahedron, so it signals that number.

clue.text: More stupid to accept golf competitively

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: inaner means sillier, more stupid
G is golf in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: It is more foolish to take up golf as a competitive sport.
explanation.walkthrough: 'golf' looks like the sport the surface is about, but it is the radio code for G. The phrase is used of something done for real, as in 'first shot fired in anger'.
explanation.definitionFit: Playing in anger means in a real match, not practice: the idiom covers serious, competitive action.

clue.text: Decided to secure zip? Cold outside

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast inside, so one word encloses the others

parts.note: someone decided is sure of their view
FA is short for sweet FA, meaning nothing or zip
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: Someone has chosen to fasten a zip because it is cold out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'zip' looks like a fastener but means nothing, FA. 'outside' seems to belong with 'Cold' but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The surface of a thing is its exterior, the outside layer.
